messages:
ellie (product): quick sync — we need a tight framing for the pricing roadmap sprint. customers keep asking for reserved capacity + flexible burst; sales wants simple tiers. can we choose a prioritization framework and a launch checklist?

sam (eng): +1. RICE feels useful but we also need deployment complexity in the effort side. suggested fields: user reach, revenue impact, infra complexity, risk.

maria (sales): from field: 3 enterprise customers will only sign if we have a dedicated commit + predictable rate limits. they also want burst credits for traffic spikes. worth flagging as hard requirement for deals in pipeline.

anil (data): we can estimate usage patterns to model unit economics. quick ask: can product pick a small set of representative customers so we can run simulations?

sophie (finance): need to see modeled ARR lift vs margin delta. reserved capacity increases committed revenue but raises cost if utilization is low. burst credits complicate billing calculus.

ellie (product): proposal: use a tweaked RICE: Reach, Impact, Complexity (infra+billing), Effort. keep score 1-10 and force a qualitative risk note. quick scoring template: 
```
R: 1-10 (how many customers/percent of revenue)
I: 1-10 (lift to conversion/ARR)
C: 1-10 (infra + billing complexity)
E: 1-10 (eng + product effort)
Score = (R * I) / (C * E)
```

sam (eng): also add a deployment sequencing column: can we ship payg rate-limiting primitives first, then reserved capacity? smaller rollout reduces risk.

maria (sales): that sequencing helps — if payg rate limits are live we can anchor tiers and then sell reserved as an add-on. customers buying reserved want SLA and isolation promises.

anil (data): I'll prepare two workload sims: one for PLG-heavy customers and one for enterprise reserved. will include token distribution and peak patterns. need target customer list by EOD.

sophie (finance): I'll run margin scenarios. two knobs: price per token under reserved vs payg, and discount ladder by commit size. plus cost model for partially utilized GPUs.

ellie (product): launch criteria proposal: (1) core rate-limits + billing primitives implemented and tested; (2) reserved capacity allocation + simple SLA template; (3) pricing page + churn impact doc; (4) pilot with 1-2 enterprise customers; (5) alerting for underutilization.

sam (eng): tech checklist additions: autoscale safety nets, quota enforcement per-tenant, metering accuracy to 1%. need a canary path in Redwood Dedicated infra.

maria (sales): I'll coordinate pilot customers. also request a simple one-pager for AE talking points and migration playbook for customers on payg -> reserved.

ellie (product): decision needed: do we prioritize reserved-capacity path (higher immediate revenue, higher infra work) or payg/tiering (broader reach, lower infra lift)? score these on the template and we'll vote tomorrow.

anil (data): I'll publish sims in #product-data by midday.

sophie (finance): finance will add the ARR/margin sheet and sensitivity to utilization.

sam (eng): estimating effort: payg rate limits + billing primitives = 3 sprints; reserved capacity + SLA + autoscale = 4-5 sprints. can we split teams?

ellie (product): yes — propose parallel tracks: core billing primitives first (shared infra), reserved capacity as a focused project with an SRE lead. sync at weekly planning.

maria (sales): 👍 will slot pilot customers for the reserved track.

deploy-bot: Deployment note: staging feature-branch created for rate-limiter primitives — build/CI green: https://ci.redwood.internal/12345

ellie (product): ok everyone — action items: anil: sims + customer list; sam: detailed sprint plan & API contract; sophie: financial scenarios; maria: pilot commitments; I'll consolidate scores and run the RICE vote tomorrow. thanks! :rocket:
